name: Research companies and make active equity portfolio decisions
summary: Active Equities teams in the Americas, Europe and Asia research listed companies and decide to open, add to, trim or exit positions in a concentrated long/short, market-neutral portfolio. Most decisions start from results or news on a held name and take a few days; new positions need weeks of modelling, management meetings, expert calls and a team review. Every decision then passes through an optimiser that sizes the trade and hedges unwanted factor exposures, and a department limit check, before orders go to the central trading desk. Waiting for management meetings, weekly team reviews and earnings-season bunching drive elapsed time; inside information controls and optimiser reruns add steps.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager whose 137-person Active Equities department runs fundamental long/short public equity portfolios with internal teams.
baseline.notes: Relationship investments and pre-IPO deals follow a separate private-style process (ae-ri-source-diligence) and are excluded.

unit_of_work: one portfolio decision (new position, add, trim or exit)
trigger: A new idea or an event on a held company (results, news, price move, risk flag) prompts a review.
end_state: A recorded portfolio decision with target size and hedges is sent to order capture, or the review ends with no action (idea dropped, hold, or name restricted).

volume.seasonality: Peaks in the four earnings seasons (late January to February, late April to May, late July to August, late October to November).

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate; the fund does not publish decision counts. About 300 order-producing decisions a month across five teams fits a concentrated book of a C$74 billion gross portfolio.

steps.name: Log the trigger for a decision
steps.description: A trigger for a portfolio decision reaches the team: a new idea from screens, conferences or broker research, or an event on a held name such as quarterly results, a price move through a target, news or a risk report flag. The trigger is noted on the team's coverage list.

evidence.note: Analysts both generate ideas and monitor holdings (Financial Edge); the split of cases is the author's estimate for a concentrated book with roughly 15 to 20 new positions a month.

steps.name: Screen the idea and check restricted lists
steps.description: An analyst pulls financials, valuation multiples, liquidity, ownership and existing fund exposure from Bloomberg and the data platform, checks the name against the restricted and watch lists in the compliance system, and writes a one-page summary for the portfolio manager.

error.defect_description: Missed existing exposure elsewhere in the fund or wrong liquidity figure.

control.basis: Insider trading law and the fund's Code of Conduct: restricted and watch list check before research contact with a company

evidence.note: Universe prescreen is the first step of the bottom-up process (CFA); restricted lists for names with inside information (SEC risk alert summary). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether to research the idea
steps.description: The portfolio manager reads the summary, compares the idea with the team's pipeline, mandate and current exposures, and decides at the weekly team meeting or by message whether an analyst should spend time on full research.

evidence.note: Weekly team meetings on holdings and opportunities (Financial Edge); share pursued is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the financial model and valuation
steps.description: A senior associate studies filings, industry data and competitors, builds or rebuilds a three-statement model with scenarios, and turns the forecasts into a target price and expected return for the long or short case.

evidence.note: Industry and business understanding, forecasts and target price are steps in the CFA bottom-up process; hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Meet company management
steps.description: The senior associate requests a meeting through investor relations or a broker conference, prepares questions, meets management (in person or by video), and writes up notes, taking care not to receive material non-public information. If inside information is received, the name is restricted and the work stops.

error.defect_description: Meeting notes miss a key risk.

control.basis: Selective disclosure rules (U.S. Regulation FD, Canadian National Policy 51-201) and insider trading law: no material non-public information in management meetings

next.condition: enough evidence to write the thesis

evidence.note: Analysts speak with management under strict disclosure rules (Financial Edge); waits for meetings and the shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pre-clear expert network calls
steps.description: A compliance officer reviews the request to speak with industry experts through an expert network, checks that the experts are not current employees of the company or bound by confidentiality, and approves the calls with standard compliance reminders and a log entry.

control.basis: Policies to prevent misuse of material non-public information: logging and review of expert network communications (SEC April 2022 risk alert expectations; fund MNPI policy)

evidence.note: Documenting and reviewing expert network communications is expected (SEC alert summary); pre-clearance by Compliance is common practice. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold expert calls and channel checks
steps.description: An associate schedules and holds calls with former employees, customers or suppliers arranged by the expert network, and checks channel data, then summarises what the calls show about demand, pricing and competitors.

error.defect_description: Unrepresentative expert view given too much weight.

evidence.note: Use of expert networks is common practice; call count and waits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review material ESG factors
steps.description: A Sustainable Investing specialist reviews the company against the industry materiality framework, checks disclosures, controversies and climate exposure, and sends a short note on material sustainability risks for the thesis.

control.basis: Sustainable investing policy: material sustainability factors reviewed for significant public equity investments

evidence.note: Research reports identify material sustainability risks for significant investments in public companies (2022 report); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the investment thesis
steps.description: The senior associate writes the thesis: business, variant view, valuation and target price, catalysts, key risks, ESG points, bear case, proposed size and exit triggers, and files it in the team's research repository.

evidence.note: Analysts prepare detailed reports on their view of a company (Financial Edge); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Team review of the thesis
steps.description: At the weekly team meeting the senior associate presents the thesis and the portfolio manager and colleagues challenge assumptions, valuation and risks. The portfolio manager approves, asks for more work or rejects the idea.

control.basis: Team investment review of new positions under AE investment process

next.condition: approved within the portfolio manager's authority
approved but above the portfolio manager's authority

evidence.note: Findings are challenged in an investment committee (Financial Edge); outcome shares are the author's estimate. Only the portfolio manager's time is counted although several people attend.

steps.name: Group head approves a large new position
steps.description: For a position above the portfolio manager's size authority, the group head reads the thesis and the proposed size, discusses risks with the team and approves, approves a smaller size, sends it back or declines.

control.basis: Delegated investment authorities under the investment policies, standards and procedures required by the fund's governing act s.35

evidence.note: The Act requires investment policies, standards and procedures; AE size authorities are not public and the share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the model after results or news
steps.description: An associate reads the results release, filing or news, updates the model and estimates, compares the numbers with the thesis and consensus, and flags whether the thesis still holds.

evidence.note: Models change most often in earnings season (Financial Edge); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Recommend add, trim, hold or exit
steps.description: The senior associate writes a short note comparing the price with the target, the updated estimates and the thesis milestones, and recommends adding, trimming, holding or exiting, with a suggested size change.

error.defect_description: Recommendation anchored on the old thesis.

evidence.note: Rebalancing under a buy and sell discipline (CFA); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide on the position
steps.description: The portfolio manager reads the note, checks the position's weight and contribution to risk, and decides to add, trim, exit or hold, or asks for a full re-underwrite if the thesis looks broken.

evidence.note: Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the optimiser to size the trade and hedge factors
steps.description: The portfolio strategy associate runs the portfolio optimiser with the new target weight, the risk model and constraints on gross and net exposure, country, sector and style factors, liquidity and trading cost, and produces the proposed single-name trade and the hedging trades.

error.defect_description: Wrong constraint or stale holdings give an unintended exposure.

evidence.note: AE assembles positions through an optimisation that removes unintended factor exposures (F2022); optimisation with factor constraints is described by CFA. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review proposed size and factor exposures
steps.description: The portfolio manager checks the optimiser's proposal: whether the hedges keep the intended single-name bet, the resulting factor and country exposures, liquidity in days of volume and expected trading cost, and accepts it or changes constraints for a rerun.

evidence.note: Long/short construction trades risk reduction against cost and complexity (CFA); rerun share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check department risk limits and liquidity
steps.description: The portfolio strategy associate checks the post-trade portfolio against department limits on potential loss, gross and net exposure, single-name concentration and liquidity, and flags any breach or any single-name short that needs a borrow check.

control.basis: Department risk limits within the fund's risk appetite framework

next.condition: single-name short needs a borrow check

evidence.note: Investment policies and limits required by the Act; check content and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve a limit exception or require a resize
steps.description: A director reviews the breach, the rationale and the expected duration, and either approves a temporary exception with conditions or asks for a smaller trade or extra hedge.

control.basis: Limit exceptions approved above the portfolio manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check borrow availability and cost for a single-name short
steps.description: An associate asks the prime brokers for availability and the borrow fee, checks recall risk and short interest, and confirms whether the short can be held at an acceptable cost.

next.condition: too costly; rerun with another hedge

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the decision and instruct order entry
steps.description: The portfolio manager records the decision in the decision log with rationale, target size and urgency, and enters or instructs the orders for the single-name trade and its hedges, which go to order capture and pre-trade compliance.

control.basis: Decision record kept for investment oversight and internal audit

evidence.note: Trade urgency follows the alpha horizon and portfolio managers work with traders on strategy (CFA); time is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Inside information received
exceptions.description: Management or an adviser discloses inside information; the name goes on the restricted list and research stops until it is public.

exceptions.name: Thesis broken on a held name
exceptions.description: Results contradict the thesis, so the position is re-underwritten from the model up before the add, trim or exit decision.

exceptions.name: Optimiser rerun
exceptions.description: The optimiser's hedges dilute the intended bet or create an unwanted exposure, so constraints are changed and the run repeated.

exceptions.name: Department limit breach
exceptions.description: The trade would breach a department limit; a director approves an exception or the trade is resized.

exceptions.name: Short not borrowable at acceptable cost
exceptions.description: A single-name short is too costly or scarce to borrow, so another hedge or a smaller position is used.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trigger to recorded decision or no-action
benchmarks.population: Fundamental long/short equity decisions at a large institutional investor

evidence.note: No published statistic. Author's estimate: reviews of held names close within a few days around weekly team meetings, new positions take four to eight weeks of research and review; because new ideas are only about 12% of cases the 90th percentile falls in the slower held-name reviews and the earliest new-idea outcomes.
Gross assets C$74 billion.
137 full-time employees.

benchmarks.unit: CAD, fiscal 2021 (including C$63 million transaction costs and C$225 million operating expenses)

evidence.note: C$303 million in costs.

pain_points.description: Results for most holdings arrive in a few weeks each quarter, so model updates and position reviews bunch up and queues lengthen in earnings season.

evidence.note: Earnings season is when analysts most often change models (Financial Edge).

pain_points.description: Management meetings and expert calls depend on outside calendars and take one to three weeks to arrange.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: The optimiser's hedges can dilute or distort the intended single-name bet, so portfolio managers rerun it with new constraints.

evidence.note: Optimisation to remove unintended factor exposures (F2022); long/short adds cost and complexity (CFA).

pain_points.description: Emerging market names carry regulatory risk that company models miss; regulatory changes in China caused AE's fiscal 2022 loss.

evidence.note: Loss resulting from unanticipated regulatory changes in China (F2022).

pain_points.description: Controls on inside information (restricted lists, expert call pre-clearance and logging) add waits and can stop research on a name.

evidence.note: SEC 2022 expectations on expert networks and restricted lists.

sources.title: 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing

sources.title: Active Equity Investing: Portfolio Construction (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Building blocks: rewarded factor exposures (overweight, underweight or neutralise), alpha skill, position sizing and breadth; portfolio construction as optimisation with an objective function and constraints on concentration, factor exposures, leverage and liquidity; long/short trades risk reduction against cost and complexity

sources.title: Active Equity Investing: Strategies (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Bottom-up process: define and prescreen the universe, understand the industry and business, forecast financial performance, convert forecasts to a target price, construct the portfolio and rebalance under a buy and sell discipline; fundamental analysis examines business model, competitive advantage, management and governance

sources.title: Trade Strategy and Execution (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Alpha decay drives trade urgency; portfolio managers need to work closely with traders to set trading strategy; order size judged against average daily volume

sources.title: SEC's Division of Examinations Issues Risk Alert Regarding MNPI and Code of Ethics Compliance
sources.supports: SEC April 2022 risk alert: advisers must have policies reasonably designed to prevent misuse of material non-public information, including documenting and reviewing communications with expert network consultants, due diligence on alternative data providers, and restricted lists for securities about which the adviser has inside information

sources.title: A Day in the Life of an Investment Research Analyst
sources.supports: Buy-side analysts generate ideas and monitor holdings, update models and estimates, change models most often in earnings season, speak to management after results under strict disclosure rules, write detailed reports challenged in an investment committee, and hold weekly team meetings on holdings and opportunities

sources.title: the fund's governing act (S.C. 1997, c. 40), sections 34 and 35
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: The board must establish investment policies, standards and procedures that a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in dealing with the property of others, and the Board and its subsidiaries must follow them; the investment committee requires procedures to monitor compliance with investment policies

assumptions: Cases include reviews that end with no trade (idea dropped, hold, restricted); about 77% of cases end in an order-producing decision, which then becomes several orders across days, accounts and hedges in mkt-order-capture.
New ideas are 12% of cases and events on held names 88%; these shares, the outcome shares and all hands-on times are the author's estimates.
ae_bm stands in for the Research & Portfolio Strategy group named in the F2021 report, which runs portfolio construction; the organisation file has no separate role for it.
The team review step counts only the portfolio manager's time although several team members attend; the extra meeting time is part of the unrecorded load behind the stated FTE.
Stated FTE is set above the FTE implied by hands-on time because analysts and portfolio managers also spend time on reading, conferences and monitoring that does not attach to one decision.
Large positions need group head (ae_md) approval and limit exceptions need a director; AE's actual size authorities are not public.
compliance_officer is an organisation role not listed for this process; it is added for expert call pre-clearance. ae_smd is listed but takes no per-decision step.
Relationship investments and pre-IPO stakes, which go to the Portfolio Execution Committee, follow ae-ri-source-diligence and are excluded.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file and include large incentive pay.
